import re

# Named groups: each token type is a named group
TOKEN_SPEC = [
    ("NUMBER",   r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?"),
    ("KEYWORD",  r"\b(?:if|else|while|let|print|true|false)\b"),
    ("IDENT",    r"[A-Za-z_]\w*"),
    ("GE",       r">="), ("LE", r"<="), ("EQ", r"=="), ("NE", r"!="),
    ("ASSIGN",   r"="),
    ("GT",       r">"),  ("LT", r"<"),
    ("PLUS",     r"\+"), ("MINUS", r"-"), ("STAR", r"\*"), ("SLASH", r"/"),
    ("LPAREN",   r"\("), ("RPAREN", r"\)"),
    ("LBRACE",   r"\{"), ("RBRACE", r"\}"),
    ("SEMI",     r";"),
    ("SKIP",     r"[ \t\n]+"),
    ("COMMENT",  r"#[^\n]*"),
    ("ERROR",    r"."),
]

MASTER = re.compile("|".join(f"(?P<{name}>{pat})" for name, pat in TOKEN_SPEC))

def lex(source):
    line, line_start = 1, 0
    for m in MASTER.finditer(source):
        kind = m.lastgroup
        lexeme = m.group()
        col = m.start() - line_start + 1
        if kind == "SKIP":
            line += lexeme.count("\n")
            if "\n" in lexeme:
                line_start = m.end() - len(lexeme) + lexeme.rfind("\n") + 1
            continue
        if kind == "COMMENT":
            continue
        if kind == "ERROR":
            raise SyntaxError(f"line {line}, col {col}: unexpected {lexeme!r}")
        yield (kind, lexeme, line, col)

src = """let count = 0;
while (count <= 10) {
    count = count + 1;
}
print count;"""

for tok in lex(src):
    print(tok)
description: You can follow a master pattern from token names to located output tuples.

steps.description: TOKEN_SPEC pairs each token name with a pattern. You combine them into named groups in MASTER.
lex reads each match's group name, text and column. Whitespace updates position tracking, and comments pass through without yielding a token.

steps.answer: It contains kind, lexeme, line and col. The error branch instead raises SyntaxError with the unexpected text and its location.
